I've been experimenting with pi 3 and I'm amazed at the execution of the device and software. It works! I formatted my own sd card, installed apache and php and was turning leds on and off in just a few hours. I added some switches to gpio. I thought the pi zero was cool too before the WiFi model. Now I'm going to buy a few of the pi zero with WiFi. This great!

No contest that the pi3 is a great little powerhouse for general computing tasks but Pi zeros are just not nearly as capable. Zeros are really for once off single shot projects where you'd use a Pi2 or Pi3 but want something smaller and cheaper but need something a little more human interfacing or just a lot more processing flexibility than an ordinary microcontroller could offer. You won't be disappointed if you keep your expectations relatively low.

Make sure if you are going to connect a lot of usb devices that you've got a powered usb hub, zeros are a bit iffy when you are running a lot on the USB ports because of some pretty tight current draw limitations and for the love of god make sure you have a good read and write speed on your SD card (you also need a different OS version spesifically for Pi1 / Zero so you can't swap SD cards between your 3 and a Zero) if you're going to use it for any serious work.

I'm going to wait for a Pi Zero 2 or whatever comes next in that form factor, it really needs a better CPU and a little more RAM, trying to write code on the gen1 Zero I got (before the camera connector was integrated) was tedious as fuck and the USB problems I encountered was extremely irritating. It does do a really good job with OpenELEC though, thats its saving grace for me.

Oh and before I forget you have to actually tweak some options to make the CPU in a Zero run at 1ghz, its not a big deal to do this and it does makes a substantial difference.
